title: When the Aftermath Sings
premise: Bram Quintana, once a celebrated composition prodigy who abandoned music after a devastating loss, returns to the crumbling Aldergate Conservatory as a night janitor, cataloguing the building's silences as carefully as they once catalogued notes. When a radio broadcast airs a song Bram wrote for their late mentor and never recorded, the past becomes impossible to outrun: someone is playing it, and the conservatory is slated for demolition in six weeks. As Bram traces the song's reappearance through old rivals, estranged family, and a young student who reminds them of who they used to be, they must finally speak the goodbye they swallowed years ago. The novel ends on demolition day, with Bram performing the unfinished piece aloud in the empty concert hall as the walls come down around them—grief transmuted at last into music that belongs to no one and everyone.
about_author: Cyrus Whitlock is a former conservatory custodian turned novelist whose work explores the quiet lives built inside institutions. They live near a decommissioned music school and still sweep its steps every morning.

chapters.title: Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Introduces Bram's nocturnal routine mopping the conservatory's halls, their mental catalogue of unspoken words, and the demolition notice taped to the entrance. Emotional beat: numb competence masking grief.

chapters.title: The Radio at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A late-night radio program plays a melody Bram composed for their mentor Odile Voss and never wrote down or recorded. Shock cracks open the careful silence. Emotional beat: vertigo—the impossible made audible.

chapters.title: Six Weeks
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram calculates the timeline between the broadcast and the demolition date, deciding to find the source before the building—and the song's meaning—is erased. Emotional beat: reluctant purpose.

chapters.title: The Student Who Hums
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram notices seventeen-year-old Nell Ferro humming fragments of the song in the practice wing, the first person to hear them hum along in years. Emotional beat: recognition, unwelcome tenderness.

chapters.title: What Odile Kept
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell reveals she found a reel-to-reel tape in Odile's sealed office, recorded secretly before Odile's death. She doesn't know whose music it is. Emotional beat: innocent detonation.

chapters.title: A History of Leaving
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Flashback chapter: Bram's rise as a prodigy, Odile's mentorship, and the quarrel the night before Odile's stroke—Bram walked out mid-argument and never said goodbye. Emotional beat: guilt given architecture.

chapters.title: The Rival Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram confronts Marcus Ilić, now the conservatory's interim director and once Bram's rival, who reveals he fought to keep the building standing—and knows more about the tape than he admits. Emotional beat: old wounds, new alliances forming.

chapters.title: Listening Alone
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Alone in the archive room, Bram plays the tape: Odile's voice introducing 'the last thing my student gave me.' Bram cannot finish listening. Emotional beat: grief ambushing the guarded.

chapters.title: Nell's Audition
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell prepares to audition with the mystery piece for a scholarship that dies with the building, asking Bram—whom she suspects was a musician—for help. Bram refuses. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Brother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram visits their estranged brother Teo, who kept a ledger of every promise their family broke, including Bram's disappearance after Odile's death. Emotional beat: accountability arriving without absolution.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram tracks the broadcast to a pirate radio host, Junie, who found the tape duplicated among Odile's donated effects and has been airing it weekly. Emotional beat: the private becoming public, outrage softening into awe.

chapters.title: Who Owns a Song
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus argues the piece should be archived under Bram's name before demolition; Bram insists it belongs to Odile. Their argument exposes how each has carried the loss differently. Emotional beat: rivalry transfigured into shared mourning.

chapters.title: Practice Room 4
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Nell finds Bram playing the piece from memory in Practice Room 4 at dawn—the first time they've touched a piano in eleven years. Neither speaks of it. Emotional beat: the body remembering what the mind forbade.

chapters.title: The Letter Under the Floorboard
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Demolition surveyors pull up floorboards; beneath one in Odile's office lies an unsent letter addressed to Bram. Nell takes it but hesitates to deliver it. Emotional beat: dread of the truth.

chapters.title: Reading by Wrecking Light
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Nell gives Bram the letter. Odile forgave Bram that final night and asked them to finish the piece—to give it an ending. Bram reads it aloud once, alone, voice breaking. Emotional beat: devastation as permission.

chapters.title: Objections
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram tries to stop the demolition through petitions and calls, failing everywhere, while the town debates the building's fate. Emotional beat: futility sharpening resolve.

chapters.title: Teo Comes to Sweep
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. Teo arrives unannounced and helps Bram clean the concert hall one last time, the brothers working in wordless rhythm, the ledger closed without ceremony. Emotional beat: reconciliation without apology.

chapters.title: The Last Broadcast
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Junie announces the final airing of the song and invites whoever wrote it to claim it on air. Bram listens, pen in hand, and writes the ending Odile requested. Emotional beat: courage assembling itself.

chapters.title: Demolition Eve
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram asks Marcus to delay the crews by one hour and asks Nell to turn pages. Preparations, fear, and a sleepless night among the instruments being crated away. Emotional beat: trembling readiness.

chapters.title: Out Loud
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Climax: in the gutted concert hall, before excavators and a small gathered crowd, Bram performs the completed piece and speaks the goodbye to Odile aloud—naming every unsaid thing. Emotional beat: catharsis, grief sung rather than swallowed.

chapters.title: Rubble, Radio
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. The walls come down as Junie broadcasts the performance citywide. Nell receives the scholarship endowed in both Odile's and Bram's names. Emotional beat: inheritance passing forward.

chapters.title: When the Aftermath Sings
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Months later, Bram teaches composition part-time at a community center, keeps janitorial hours out of love rather than hiding, and hears a stranger whistling the piece. Emotional beat: belonging, finally, in the aftermath.
